answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when every identity must prove a steady pulse of real work before it can trade: each completed task earns a signed receipt, and the receipts form a cipher-chained ledger that randomly assigned peers audit, so one forged entry breaks the chain. New accounts also lock a refundable deposit in a sable escrow vault, slashed on forgery. A thousand fake identities cost a thousand deposits and a thousand verified jobs, so forgery pays less than honest work.
